findings.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/models/blocked_email.rb:11 — `should_block?` looks up `where(email: email)` with an exact, case-sensitive match and nothing normalizes (downcase/strip) the submitted email, so variants like `Spammer@evil.com` bypass a stored `spammer@evil.com` block on case-sensitive databases (Postgres); input and stored values should be normalized before comparison

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274 — the client adds the address to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present, but the server returns all email errors there (including 'has already been taken' from the new uniqueness validation and 'not allowed from that email provider'), so those addresses are permanently flagged with the generic `user.email.invalid` message, hiding the real reason after the one-time flash; gate on the blocked-email error specifically or surface the actual server message

[Medium/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 — `match_count += 1` followed by a full `record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent validations of the same email lose increments and overwrite each other with stale rows; use an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` instead

[Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — the validator performs DB writes as a side effect (SELECT plus `record.save`, re-running that record's validations and bumping `updated_at`) every time any User with a changed email is validated (signups, retries, admin edits, any `valid?` pre-check), so `match_count`/`last_match_at` no longer measure real signup attempts, and the ignored `save` return value means stats failures are silent; validators should be side-effect-free with attempt tracking in the controller or at minimum an unchecked atomic update

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:70 — the rejection match is `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` against the raw typed input, but the stored entry is the server-echoed `result.values.email`; if the server normalizes email before persisting/validating, or the user retries with different case/whitespace, the exact string comparison never matches and the client-side invalid state silently fails to appear; normalize on both sides of this contract

[Medium/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — `BlockedEmail` is stubbed and only the blocked/not-blocked branch is exercised; the moved whitelist/blacklist logic (including the refactor from `self.email =~ regexp` to `value =~ regexp`) has no unit coverage, and there is no spec pinning the new `errors`/`values` JSON shape returned by `UsersController#create` on failure, which the JS depends on, so a rename breaks the feature silently

[Low/data] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `action_type` is `null: false` with no schema-level default; the default exists only in the model's `before_validation` callback, so bulk/manual loads into `blocked_emails` (the workflow the spec comment explicitly describes) fail unless every row supplies the value; add a `default:` in the migration

[Low/doc_defect] app/models/blocked_email.rb / migration — the PR ships the blocked-email check with no admin UI, seed, API, or documentation that ever creates a `BlockedEmail` record; the only description of the intended workflow is a comment inside the spec ('If we manually load the table...'), leaving the feature inert and undiscoverable; document the intended population workflow or provide the entry point

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274 — the client adds the address to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present, but the server returns all email errors there (including 'has already been taken' from the new uniqueness validation and 'not allowed from that email provider'), so those addresses are permanently flagged with the generic `user.email.invalid` message, hiding the real reason after the one-time flash; gate on the blocked-email error specifically or surface the actual server message

adjudication.rationale: In create_account_controller.js, on failed signup it unconditionally pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails whenever `result.errors && result.errors.email` is present (new code around line ~274). The server now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash`, which will include email errors for multiple causes (e.g., `validates :email, ... uniqueness: true` in user.rb, and EmailValidator errors for not_allowed/blocked). The emailValidation computed property then short-circuits any email in `rejectedEmails` to a generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, so a non-blocked failure like "has already been taken" or "not allowed" gets permanently treated as generic invalid for that entered address within the modal, masking the true reason after the initial flash. The diff shows no gating on the specific 'blocked' case or surfacing the server-provided error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 — the validator performs DB writes as a side effect (SELECT plus `record.save`, re-running that record's validations and bumping `updated_at`) every time any User with a changed email is validated (signups, retries, admin edits, any `valid?` pre-check), so `match_count`/`last_match_at` no longer measure real signup attempts, and the ignored `save` return value means stats failures are silent; validators should be side-effect-free with attempt tracking in the controller or at minimum an unchecked atomic update

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13). `should_block?` does a query and, when a record exists, mutates and `save`s it (`match_count += 1`, `last_match_at = ...`, `record.save` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-16). Since this validator is hooked into `User` email validation (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` in app/models/user.rb), any `valid?`/save attempt with a changed email will perform these DB writes, potentially multiple times per user action and in contexts beyond actual signup attempts; the `save` return value is ignored so failed updates are silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:70 — the rejection match is `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` against the raw typed input, but the stored entry is the server-echoed `result.values.email`; if the server normalizes email before persisting/validating, or the user retries with different case/whitespace, the exact string comparison never matches and the client-side invalid state silently fails to appear; normalize on both sides of this contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a client-side cache of rejected emails: it stores `result.values.email` from the server response (`users_controller.rb` adds `values: user.attributes.slice(...)`) and later checks it via exact string match `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` where `email` is `this.get("accountEmail")`. There is no normalization (trim/downcase) on either side in the shown diff, so the cache may not trigger if the user re-enters the same address with different casing/whitespace. However, this does not create a clearly broken behavior—server-side validation will still fail and show an error; it mainly affects the UX optimization of short-circuiting validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — `BlockedEmail` is stubbed and only the blocked/not-blocked branch is exercised; the moved whitelist/blacklist logic (including the refactor from `self.email =~ regexp` to `value =~ regexp`) has no unit coverage, and there is no spec pinning the new `errors`/`values` JSON shape returned by `UsersController#create` on failure, which the JS depends on, so a rename breaks the feature silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior without corresponding coverage: `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` now contains the moved whitelist/blacklist restriction logic (previously in `User#email_validator`) plus new `BlockedEmail.should_block?` logic, but `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only exercises the blocked/not-blocked branch by stubbing `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and does not assert whitelist/blacklist behavior or the `value =~ regexp` path. Separately, `UsersController#create` now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice(...)`, and the JS change relies on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to populate `rejectedEmails`; there is no spec pinning that failure JSON shape, so a key rename/regression could break the client feature without test detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — `action_type` is `null: false` with no schema-level default; the default exists only in the model's `before_validation` callback, so bulk/manual loads into `blocked_emails` (the workflow the spec comment explicitly describes) fail unless every row supplies the value; add a `default:` in the migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `blocked_emails.action_type` with `null: false` and no DB-level `default` (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb), while the only defaulting occurs in the model via `before_validation :set_defaults` (app/models/blocked_email.rb). Inserts that bypass model validations/callbacks (e.g., bulk/manual SQL loads) would indeed fail unless `action_type` is provided, which aligns with the spec comment about manually loading the table. This is a legitimate schema/ops robustness concern, but the app path using ActiveRecord would still work, so it’s more of an improvement than a user-facing defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `blocked_emails` table/migration, `BlockedEmail` model, and integrates it into `EmailValidator` (`BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`), but this PR does not add any admin UI, API/controller endpoints, seeds, or documentation for creating/managing `BlockedEmail` records. The only hint of population workflow is an inline comment in `spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb` about manually loading the table. This makes the feature effectively undiscoverable/inert unless someone uses the DB/console, which is a legitimate completeness/documentation concern but not a correctness bug in the code shown.
